Synopsis:
    European heatwaves are imposing measurable macroeconomic damage across major EU economies, estimated at €180bn in aggregate GDP losses. France faces nuclear output curtailment due to high river temperatures. Germany confronts critical Rhine freight disruption affecting industrial supply chains. Spain and Italy suffer wildfire and agricultural damage, with Italy particularly exposed via tourism and farming. Poland remains a relative outlier with limited direct impact. Structural vulnerabilities — high debt, aging populations, energy dependencies — amplify the economic risks in the medium-to-long term.
